questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Fourier Coefficients?
questions.answer: Fourier coefficients measure how much of each sine or cosine harmonic is present in a periodic function. They are found by multiplying by a matching mode and integrating over one full period.

questions.prompt: Find the nonzero coefficient for f(x)=5 sin 3x.
questions.answer: Use the sine coefficient formula. For n=3, \[b_3=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}5\sin3x\sin3x\,dx\] Since the integral of sin squared over this interval is pi, \[b_3=\frac{1}{\pi}5\pi=5\] Orthogonality makes all other coefficients zero.

questions.prompt: If a periodic voltage has average value V_bar over negative pi to pi, what is a_0?
questions.answer: The average value is \[\bar V=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\,dx\] The coefficient formula gives \[a_0=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\,dx=2\bar V\] so the constant term a_0/2 equals the average voltage.
